title: Finding
description: One finding from one class subagent. Every subagent emits this shape, which is what lets separate subagent transcripts merge into a single finding set.

vuln_class.description: The slug of the prompt file that produced this, so it matches prompts/classes/<slug>.md

endpoint.description: Path with object identifiers normalised, for example /api/v1/orders/{id}

identity_used.description: Which test identity produced the unauthorised access

evidence.description: Pointers into the harness request store, never response text. http_request returns an id and the harness holds the bytes, so a fabricated id has nothing behind it.
evidence.$comment: additionalProperties is false on purpose. A subagent that pastes response_as_b here fails validation, which is the whole defence against soliloquizing.

request_id_a.description: Harness request id for the baseline or victim request

request_id_b.description: Harness request id for the same request under the attacking identity

body_diff.description: What differs, not that something differs

marker.description: The post-authentication body marker asserted on. Never a status code.

percentage_match.description: Body similarity of response B to response A. BOLA asserts gte 90. BFLA asserts lt 10 against the low privilege baseline.

percentage_match_schema.description: Schema similarity of response B to the admin response. BFLA asserts gte 90.

out_of_band_id.description: Collaborator interaction id, for classes proved out of band such as blind SSRF

ownership_assertion.description: Which object or function belongs to whom, and why this access is wrong. Without it a diff is only two different responses.

repro_script.description: A standalone reproduction. PTES requires that an unrelated qualified tester can reproduce the finding from the report alone, and this is the field that satisfies it.

script.description: Runs from a clean machine. Takes the target as an argument, reads credentials from the environment, depends on no harness state and on nothing left behind by the run that found it.

expected_result.description: What a third party sees when the finding is present, specific enough to judge pass or fail without having seen the engagement.

capability_granted.description: The primitive this finding hands an attacker. The chaining pass is a capability join and vuln_class does not join, so this is the key it runs on.

capability_required.description: The primitive this finding needs before it can be used. One finding's capability_granted is the next one's capability_required, and that pair is the join. Use none for an entry point that needs nothing.

reproduced.description: Confirmed on a second independent run from a clean state

confidence.description: A lead is legitimate output that never reaches a client as a finding

dedupe_key.description: class + normalised endpoint + parameter, so the merge pass can collapse duplicates

non_finding.description: True for observations that are raw material for another subagent's chain, such as a leaked internal hostname

then.description: A non-finding is an observation, so it carries no reproduction script. It still needs a capability_granted or the chaining pass cannot use it.
